versions.name: RXV2-0.9.813-the-update-record
versions.notes: One spelling of the name everywhere: LockDownRadioControl. And the receiver now keeps its own record of the last update - what it was, what it was asked to become, and how far it got - so the update page can SAY whether it worked instead of leaving you to work it out by reloading and reading the version. A failed one names the stage it stopped at and reminds you the old firmware is untouched.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.812-role-decides-itself
versions.notes: A board with no transceivers now works out for itself whether it is a Rotorflight dongle or a simulator interface. It listens on D5 first, which is the safe test - a flight controller says nothing until asked, while a receiver chatters at once - and only calls itself a dongle when nothing is talking there. A dongle that never hears a flight controller listens again every fifteen seconds, in case the receiver's transmitter was simply off at the start, and restarts into the other role when it hears one. The role card keeps Always a dongle and Always a simulator interface for anyone who wants certainty.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.811-dongle-reads-again
versions.notes: Fixes a dongle being unable to read anything from the flight controller: PIDs, rates, the lot. Since 0.9.715 a blocking read sent its request and then nothing drained the flight controller's port while it waited, so every page read timed out after 2.7 seconds - while the receiver's own background probes, pumped by the main loop, were answered normally. A wait now keeps alive the link it is waiting on: flying on a receiver, draining the flight controller's UART and USB on a dongle, without ever writing to it.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.810-simulator-switch-tells-the-truth
versions.notes: On a simulator-interface board the Simulator switch could not turn simulator mode off - the role forces it on at every boot - yet the page said it had. It now offers the thing that was wanted instead: one tap makes the board a Rotorflight dongle. The receiver refuses the impossible setting plainly, and a board with no radios is no longer offered Bind.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.809-same-icons-as-the-pages
versions.notes: The app's buttons now carry the same icons as the receiver's own pages: the helicopter and aeroplane from Fly now, the game controller from Simulator, and so on. The hand-drawn helicopter is gone - the front page already had the right one.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.808-better-helicopter
versions.notes: The helicopter on the Receiver demo is redrawn as a filled silhouette - nose, tapering tail boom, swept fin, rotor and skids - which reads far better at icon size than the outline did.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.807-helicopter-joins-the-aeroplane
versions.notes: The Receiver demo now shows a helicopter beside the aeroplane. Apple's symbol set has no helicopter, so it is drawn in the same white line weight as the symbols around it rather than dropped in as a coloured emoji.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.806-no-uninvited-back
versions.notes: Android: the app no longer walks you back to the front screen on its own. A link going idle used to do that, so the Connect page vanished before its message could be read. It now happens only when leaving a model's pages - anywhere else you leave when you choose to.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.805-nothing-found-says-so
versions.notes: Connect now says No receivers or dongles found nearby after twelve quiet seconds, with what to check, instead of leaving a spinner or an empty page. Android's back chevron is drawn rather than typed, so it sits in the middle of its circle whatever the font does.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.804-backdrop-not-stretched
versions.notes: Android: the flying-field photograph keeps its proportions. It was being stretched to the screen's shape, which squeezed a landscape picture on a tall phone; it is now cropped instead, as on iPhone.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.803-bigger-chevron
versions.notes: Android: the back chevron is drawn larger, so it carries the same weight as the question mark beside it - a thin glyph needs more point size than a letter to look the same.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.802-android-back-button-visible
versions.notes: Android: the back button on each page now sits on a solid white disc like the question mark beside it. It was there all along, but a thin blue chevron straight on the photograph could not be seen.

rotorflight.line: Rotorflight 2.3 — the release these pages are written and tested against.
